newsitem.title: USA: NRC approves Enron, Portland Gen merger.
newsitem.headline: NRC approves Enron, Portland Gen merger.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approved the merger between Enron Corp and Portland General Corp, the Oregon company said Friday.
The NRC's approval was needed because of Portland General's ownership of the Trojan Nuclear Plant, located near Rainier, Ore., which was permanently shut in 1993.
The main decommissioning of the plant, which began operation in 1976, is scheduled to be completed by 2001.
In issuing its order, the NRC said the proposed merger will not affect the qualifications of Portland General as holder of the license for Trojan.
The companies received approval from the Federal Trade Commission and the Energy Facilities Citing Council last year.
The companies have also received merger approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, but clearance from the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) is still awaited.
A settlement conference with the OPUC has been scheduled for March 12, when the companies' latest rate cut proposal is expected to be the main feature of discussion.
